correctness.rationale: For fixed \(a>0\), the positive-half integrand \(A\) is pointwise smaller than the negative-half integrand \(B\), while its reciprocal is pointwise larger. Differentiating the three ratios in \(b\) therefore gives strictly positive numerators, including the extra positive term for the overlap convention. The resulting \(b\to0^+\) boundary formulas are exact. On \(0\le a\le1\) they are elementary decreasing rational functions; on \(a>1\), the substitution \(x=\arcsin(1/a)\) produces derivative factorizations with strictly increasing sign factors and exactly one zero. Thus the global infima and uniqueness in horizontal parameter follow without numerical inference. The bundled checker reproduces the constants but is not used as a substitute for proof.

value.rationale: The source frames the smaller-to-larger half-cone ratio as its concluding optimization question and explicitly flags the lack of rigorous minimality proofs. The new strict-height monotonicity lemma resolves the conjectural boundary reduction for every positive height, turning three numerical boundary candidates into global sharp infima for the complete two-parameter family under the canonical split. The exact minimum simplifications and uniqueness statements are reusable structural information, not a recomputation of a known table. The unresolved mean-width and arbitrary-split problems are kept separate.
